He becomes a prisoner of war when he falls into the hands of the enemy. When capturing a member of the enemy armed forces, the commanding officer of a unit of the armed forces of the SFRY shall take all precautionary measures for the security of the unit." Did you take any measures based on that responsibility while the operation to search the terrain was going on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to emphasise three aspects of this item 213 on the regulations of the application of the International Law of War in the Armed Forces of Yugoslavia. The first one is that an enemy soldier has to show his willingness to surrender. It has to be visible. It has to be obvious. Second of all, he becomes a prisoner of war at the moment when he falls into the hands of the enemy. In this specific case, Muslim soldiers became prisoners of war at the moment when they were in the hands of the Army Republika Srpska. And the third aspect of that, which you will find in the second paragraph, it is ordered to an officer of the armed forces of the SFRY to take all the necessary measures to secure the safety of his own unit, which means that he is responsible for the lives and well-being of his own men who are participating in capturing the enemy. I was governed by this item 213 when I issued my order as to how to proceed during the process to take prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if you could give us a sort of overview of the sort of people that your troops might have encountered in the period say the 18th to the 26th of July in the territory behind your frontlines?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When searching the terrain, the forces of the Zvornik Brigade with the reinforcements that it had at the moment, came across the elements of the 28th Division that were left behind, as well as the combat group that were infiltrated by the 2nd Corps in the rear of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was the position so far as those who wanted to walk to Nezuk were concerned during that period?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th everybody who appeared in the area could go through without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about combatants who were prepared to lay down their arms and surrender?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combatants who laid down their arms and surrendered were taken prisoners and brought to the Standard barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what about those who didn't want to surrender but wanted to fight?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some combat groups of that sort, especially supported by the groups infiltrated from the direction of the 2nd Corps. We engaged against such groups, and in that fighting some individuals lost their lives, they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What steps did you take, and I'll use the words of the article, to take precautionary measures for the security of your units during that time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew the terrain which was being searched. It was a very thick wood, very dense vegetation, high grass, a lot of crevices, brooks, and streams, and any scouring of the territory was risky activity. That's why I ordered that thing, that -- that my men should proceed with caution making sure that they were safe, and I was also counting on all sorts of perfidities [phoen] that might have been used by the enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can we move on to the 19th of July. What combat activities were going on on the 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of July there were attempts to -- of forceful breakthrough to the troops of the 4th and the 7th Battalion. Our soldiers engaged with the enemy soldiers during the scouring of the terrain and both sides sustained losses. Both the VRS as well as the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we return then to our duty operations officer's notebook. For you General Pandurevic, page 780. For the rest of us page 162. And the first entry for the 19th of July that I want to draw your attention to, but just wait until we have the document on our screens, would you. The entry reads: "At 0620 one person from the Zeljava company was killed and one was wounded. 4th Battalion. The commander of the 7th Battalion called personally and reported that information," and then there are some names, Milenko Milosevic killed, Nenad Acentic wounded? What does that reflect in relation to what was going on on the 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reference is made to the Zeljava company. It's a nickname for a company that was composed of soldiers, refugees, hailing from village Zeljava in central Bosnia. One soldier from that company was killed and another wounded on that day, and the commander of the 7th Battalion also reported the names of one fallen soldier and one wounded. And this reflects the combat operations and what was going on on the 19th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we go forward a couple of pages in that book, General Pandurevic, page 782 for you. 164 for the rest of us. Firstly the very top entry, "Another 28 were liquidated and three were captured." What does that reflect?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the scouring of the terrain, there was an armed combat, 28 enemy soldiers died or were killed and three were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you recall which of your unit were involved in that, and where that took place, or was it generally across the whole terrain?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the terrain was being scoured, the Podrinje detachment took part of the 16th Krajina Brigade, also the unit from the East Bosnia Corps, and also some units from the 4th and the 7th Battalion and their intervention platoons. I don't know the location of every particular unit for that day though. Dragan Obrenovic was heading the terrain sweep effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. You've led me on to the next question which is, where were you throughout the 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Pretty much the last entry from the 19th of July, 2239: "In the area of Staro Selo there was a contact between intervention platoon and Turks and everything is under control for the time being." Do you have any recollection of what that was about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Staro Selo is in the 7th Battalion defence sector and it was noted that there was a conflict between the intervention detachment of that unit and members of the 28th Division or infiltrated units in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, in relation to that day, can we look at P1261, A in the English, and B in the Serbian. I've got no flag to say this is under seal or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just in case we don't know this from earlier evidence, who is Colonel Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Cerovic is the assistant commander of the Drina Corps for morale and religious and political affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just, if we go through the early parts of this, he says "hello." Do you recall speaking to him on the 19th of July in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to Cerovic during that period of time several times, and had it not been for this conversation, it would be hard for me to actually confirm the date and the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. He says: "Good morning Vinko. "Good morning. How are you? "Well, I'm running around here since last night we --" something, "again. "Where? "They are up there at Crni Vrh, over there at Potocari, Planinci, the part towards Baljkovica." And he says: "Ah ha, you mean the ones who are coming out on this side; is that right? "Yes, from there. And all of them are rushing over here to us." What are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am probably talking about the sweeping of the terrain and the problems with the straggling and infiltrated groups. Not everything is written down here word for word, but that is what it refers to in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we just have a look at page 2 in the English, please. And page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where is Nisici?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nisici is an elevation or a plateau close to Sarajevo, in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps area north-east of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then we can go on down there and you said: "No, seriously, I've sent a report yesterday. You could see what kind of losses we sustained." Well, we can probably work out what report you are referring to, but Cerovic said to you: "Yes. And I presented that to Krstic and wrote him a special report based on your interim and daily reports." What did you understand was being conveyed to you there by Mr. Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cerovic was telling me that he had absolutely informed Krstic with my interim combat report of the 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now can we move on, please, to the 20th of July. What was going on the 20th of July on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of July, the terrain was scoured as also the fortification of positions along the defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at 7D93, the regular combat report of the 20th of July. 7D93. 93. That might be a good moment to take the break because that's certainly not the document I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 25 minute break now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can proceed precisely where we left off and have 7D93 in e-court. And this is the regular combat report of the 20th of July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, we can see from paragraph 2: "The R Battalion is providing permanent protection for traffic along the Orahovac-Crni Vrh road while the ground search is being performed by units of the rear Podrinje detachment, intervention units of the 7th and 4th Battalions and the 16th company of the Krajina Brigade, together with the Zvornik intervention unit of the Ministry of Interior." Is that the sort of thing that the R Battalion would routinely be used for?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this Battalion was mobilised with the intention of securing the terrain and that's what it was doing here, securing the Zvornik-Crni Vrh road, meaning that it was deployed there so that the traffic would proceed safely and without impediment, that was one of its functions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, it's a document in Cyrillic, but what is the word in Serbian used to describe what its task was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word is "Obisberdze [phoen]."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And from this document can we glean what, as it were, the main concerns and tasks of the brigade were on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the search of the terrain in the indicated area and to control and secure the road in order to smash the stragglers and infiltrated groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where were you on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And who was in command of the operation to search the terrain?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we have a look at P377, the duty officers' notebook again please. For you, General Pandurevic, page 783 and 784. The rest of us pages 165 and 6. So we'll start with page 165, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And obviously from the fact that we've got to go over the page, we're looking at the entry at the very bottom. Now, who was the duty officer on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several handwritings appear here for the 27th [as interpreted]. The only one I recognise is this one that is quite distinctive, the one by Major Galic. I don't know whether he was replaced at one point but it seems that he might have been on duty the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just, it says the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you just flick back in the book for us and confirm what date this entry is written?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we'll just have a look at this entry. "Since contact with the other side has been established through the radio communication and the other side has posed question that we are not competent to answer at our level, I suggest that competent organs from the Superior Command come to the forward command post of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade and get directly involved in the work. The other side has asked for the following: "Allowing passing of the rest of the column, exchange the prisoners from Vis for the ones captured at Lisaca and two women captured in the area of a trig point." What is the trig point? It says it's illegible, can you read it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says trig point in the Osmace sector of the tactical group from Sekovici. So it's a kilometre or two away from there, so it's between the Zvornik and the Sekovici Brigade, in between those two brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's probably not the most important aspect of this entry in the book, but what is the reference to contact with the other side through radio all about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time and after the closing of the corridor, we had contacts with the other side through our premier listening station. And as I can see here, the deputy -- the assistant Chief of Staff for operations, Dusko Vukotic, was the one who received the information because this radio listening station was under his jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he said, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the last part of your last sentence. If you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The other side or the 2nd Corps demanded radio contact with the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And this entry is written in the first person, "I suggest that competent organs from the Superior Command come to the forward command post." Whose views is this entry expressing?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that Vukotic made this proposal and sent it to Galic or someone informed me and then I conveyed it to Galic, so it was either Vukotic or myself, one of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what did you mean by "not competent to answer" and your invitation to Superior Command get directly involved, if it was yours?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, I wasn't competent for exchanges of prisoners at the level of the brigade; although, on the 16th and the 17th I did do that and tried to do that together with Semso when we are talking about soldiers from the Zvornik Brigade. After all the events that had taken place on the 16th and the 17th, I believe that it would be too much to continue to maintain contacts with the Muslim side and try to negotiate exchanges, and for that reason as far as I can remember I sent an interim combat report to the corps command pointing to this problem and asking that the corps from now on deals with these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can we just briefly go forward a couple of pages in the book, which for you, General Pandurevic, is page 785, and the rest of us page 167.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you please confirm to us firstly that we are still looking at an entry for the 20th of July? And would you explain what is meant to us by the reference there to "commission of exchange"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission of exchange -- well, this was written by the duty operations officer as a note for him to put into the regular combat report because already we had a certain number of prisoners of war and we were already thinking and seeking a way to have them exchanged or to allocate a location where they would be sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we move forward now to the 21st of July and will you turn one page forward in the duty officers' notebook to page 786. We can all go to page 168.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we see there there is an entry at 0440: "Zlatar informed that the situation is normal." But then at 0555: "The attacks started at the adjacent unit on the left - the juncture between us and Duricic (Vukotic) premier 5 - 6 network it appears to be Vis." What happened in the early hours of the 21st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our radio listening station premier discovered in time the radio networks of the 2nd Corps which were not functional before that, and on the 21st early in the morning on 5 a.m. an attack began by forces of the 2nd Corps. Perhaps the strongest force up to then that had ever carried out an attack on the Zvornik Brigade positions. Our neighbour to the left in the V section was attacked first, and then moved to our 7th and 4th Battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You said that probably the heaviest attack yet. How did the attack on the 21st of July compare with that on the morning of the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the forces engaged at the front, these were much stronger forces. All were intervention units of the 2nd Corps which previously were engaged in some other sectors of the front, but the objective at the time of the Muslim forces was to cut off the Zvornik-Snagovo road, to capture that section, and then continue the attack towards Zvornik itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what form did the attack take?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack began with artillery support, as usual, then there were infantry attacks which lasted until 12.00, and then these forces later pulled back.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How long in total did the attack go on for?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it lasted until noon with artillery firing at the same time at our positions and fire at Zvornik itself. And I think that there was some civilians who were killed and were wounded in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What effect did it have on your defence lines?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines of defence remained where they were and all the attacks were rejected.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Repelled, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go forward, please, three pages in the duty officers' notebook to page 789 for you, General Pandurevic, and the rest of us page 171.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And there's an entry there: "Stara Drina equals: 1, at market did not explode. 1, Biljana Lackovic; 2, Borka Lazarevic, Rocevic; and 3, Zoran, surname illegible, 1967. Five wounded," and at the side, "one equals two women." Who were those people and what does that entry record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was information from the duty operations officer that he received at that point in time, and Stara Drina probably means the hotel Drina. Market is a building where some shells dropped and one of them did not explode. As for the precise information about those killed and wounded can be found in the regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where were they killed and wounded?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town itself, the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We can probably tell from the names, but what sexes are those people listed as being killed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first two are women and the third is a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just to confirm the picture, can we have a look at 7D94, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see at paragraph 1, the regular combat report records that: "During the night there was enemy provocation by infantry fire. Early in the morning, the enemy carried out a strong artillery and infantry attack on the positions of the 6th, 4th and 7th Battalions. Four 82 millimetre mortar shells hit the 6th Battalion in the area of Goluboviji. Tanks, self-propelled guns, and mortars fired at Pandurica from the areas of the Ekonomija, Brdo, Zukiji, Lazareviji and Borainovac. Two soldiers were wounded." And then if we can go to the bottom of the report. There we see the same names listed as being killed in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's move on, please, by looking at P339 to help us understand what happened the following day on the 22nd of July. "In the evening, the enemy opened fire at the positions of the 4th and 7th Battalion. It also opened artillery fire at Zvornik and Velika Glavica. During the night and early in the morning enemy groups from behind the positions of the 4th and 7th tried to pass through our positions --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for slowing down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "-- and reached Muslim controlled territory. During the day the 3rd Infantry Company combed the terrain from Crni Vrh to Orahovac road to Snagovo and Kamenica." Considering that, give us an overview of what was happening on the 22nd of July after the strong attack on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less all that time after the 18th or the end of July, the forces of the 2nd Corps opened artillery fire from the frontline and in that way they allowed the elements that were left behind and that had been infiltrated to break through towards Nezuk. They were also very often there were infantry attacks to help the forces that were left behind and are trying to break through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We will come on to another document because on the 22nd of July, you sent an interim combat report, which is P340, which we can have a look at together. The original is handwritten. Whose handwriting is that, sir, General Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was written by Major Mijo Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At your dictation or at his own volition or what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I tasked him with writing it but that he himself put it together and signed on my behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see that under paragraph 1 he records "in engaging enemy groups along the Planinci-Perunika-Brezik village line, 10 enemy soldiers were liquidated, armed mostly with automatic weapons, while 23 Muslim soldiers were captured." And we look at paragraph 3: "We request from the corps command that the exchange commission start work as soon as possible. We also require instructions as to what do with the prisoners, where to put them, and to whom we should hand them over." Why did you write an interim combat report and the 22nd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that already on the 20th we had informed the corps about that, there was no reaction thus we insisted on this activity starting as soon as possible because our prison in the barracks was full of prisoners and they could no longer be kept there. I didn't know what the corps would decide, whether they would decide for them to be sent to Batkovic or perhaps Vlasenica or perhaps an exchange would be organised at the separation line in Memici, and that's why we decided to issue this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Just looking at the document, did the interim combat report on the 22nd of July have anything to do with combat?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows that the terrain had been scoured in the area referred to herein. That there were both killed and captured in combat. In other words, the first part of this report does concern combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back briefly to the duty officers' notebook, page 793 for you, General Pandurevic. For the rest of us, page 175.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And conveniently the dates at the top here, the 22nd of July. I just want to ask about two entries here, please. Firstly, the one at 0930: "A company from the 16th headed out to Trnovo from the barracks." What does that relate to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the company from the 16th Krajina Motorised Brigade from the 1st Krajina Corps. Up to that time, that company was on the strength of the Zvornik Brigade, and as far as I can remember, an order had arrived for this company to be referred to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And secondly the penultimate entry on that page: "2nd Battalion Gotovac called the commander regarding negotiations with Semso, is there anything?" Who is Gotovac and what was the call about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the person in question is Dragan Gotovac, reserve captain. His brother, relative, or somebody else had been either captured or gone missing. I kept in contact with Semso and I asked for any information about that person. Dragan Gotovac had probably asked for an update on that person as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on the 22nd of July, were you still speaking regularly to Semso Muminovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that it was regular communication. However, if he wanted to talk to me, he could via our radio surveillance device, and I could do the same if I wanted to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The entry we read on the 20th of July in which you or Mr. Vukotic expressed the view that the other side was asking questions you were not competent to answer, do you recall whether you expressed that to Semso Muminovic at any time, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. However, I do believe that the message had arrived from Semso and it that was it message for me. So it was either I who said it to Semso or actually asked Vukotic to convey the message to Semso and tell him that I could no longer be involved in that business.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If it had been down to you, General Pandurevic, if you'd had the authority, what would you have done with these prisoners at the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have organised exchange Memici at the separation line there. I would have exchanged them and sent them to the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was preventing you from doing that between the 20th of July and the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation prevented me from doing that. There was combat ongoing, and I had already done two many moves on my own at my own risk, and it would have just been too much both for me and my superiors had I done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was the situation so far as the number of prisoners you had by the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information about the number of prisoners may be found in regular combat reports in the duty officers' log-book, and even in the duty officers' log-book of the barracks. I believe that on the 23rd, the prison unit was overcrowded and those people had to be moved urgently to one of the collection centres for prisoners of war. There may have been even over 30 of them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how many were you equipped to hold?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not even a special room. It was just one part of the building that could be used to keep soldiers of the Zvornik Brigade who had been involved in a disciplinary offence or transgression so that that room, so to speak, could hold a maximum of 30 or maybe 40 people, but that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have a look, please, at P1307 at B.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And this is a record of an intercepted radio communication between apparently General Krstic and Major Bojanovic. Do you recall whether he was in fact the duty officer at Standard on the morning of the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in this intercept Major Bojanovic, Palma duty officer. Most probably he was. If were to look at the log-book, I could tell you with certainty whether he was duty operation officer on the 23rd because I know his handwriting very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, very well then. Just turn to the 23rd of July in the book you have in front of you. We won't bother getting it up on the screen, and you tell us if you can recognise Major Bojanovic's handwriting at about 6.00 in the morning of the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a log-book and the entry made on the 23rd, and the complete first page save for maybe the last two lines is indeed Ljubo Bojanovic's handwriting, which means that he was on duty on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. And he is recorded as saying to General Krstic that the detention facility is full. There are more than 30 of them as well as saying that six Turks were captured on the previous night. And does that accord with your recollection of the situation on the 22nd and early 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we now look please at P1309, A in the English and B in the Serbian which is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this conversation is the same morning, an hour and 20 minutes later if all the times are correct. And it's a conversation which apparently involves you. Do you recall having such a conversation as this on the morning of the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember having been engaged in a conversation like this, and the other person was Colonel Cerovic as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to ask you a few questions about what we see here. You apparently said: "Well, we are still catching Turks. I have some prisoners. I have some wounded, and I don't know what to do with them, where to send them?" The first question is, do you remember if you called Cerovic or he called you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you on the 23rd of July have some wounded prisoners as well as ordinary prisoners?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a group of wounded who had been brought earlier and were kept at the dispensary of the Zvornik Brigade, and I referred to them in this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And going on down the conversation you ask: "Did anybody talk about an exchange for those guys from --" is it Lisaka [phoen] or Lisaca? That's a place which appeared in the duty officers' notebook a couple of days ago? Who were the guys from Lisaca?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that on the 20th, this word, "Lisaca," had been mentioned as it was again in the report on the 22nd. These were soldiers from the East Bosnia Corps who had been captured in March or sometime earlier that year at Lisaca facility. I wanted to speed up my exchange and that's why I remembered them and mentioned them to Mr. Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the conversation goes on. You say: "Yes, yes, so does anybody know who I should send them to?" And Cerovic says: "Well, I can tell you what to do with it if there is because Begovic says he has, you know --" And you said: "Well, what about Matkovic?" Did you say Matkovic or mention Matkovic in that conversation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this conversation has not been recorded well because here when reference is made to Begovic, I must have mentioned him because he was the head of medical personnel in Zvornik. He was an MD by profession, and here where it says "Matkovic," I believe that the word I used was actually "Batkovic" which is the name where of the place where the prisoner of war camp was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So I mean, we may all recall him. There was a doctor at the Zvornik Brigade called Begovic, wasn't there. What were you saying in this conversation that linked together the name Begovic and the camp at Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I might be right but I was asking you a question. It's plain that the conversation is incomplete here. What were you saying to Mr. Cerovic about Dr. Begovic and Batkovic; what was all that about, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned Begovic, I must have mentioned the wounded as well. He was aware of their condition and he knew that they could be transported. I insisted on that future transport to include both the prisoners of war and the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now can we go to P1310, B in the B/C/S under seal, and A in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just to save a little time, General Pandurevic, would you turn in the duty officers' notebook to page 795. Now, here we have another intercept 5 minutes after the last one in which you were apparently a participant, where the participant in the previous conversation, which if that is right, must be Mr. Cerovic called and asked for Vinko again but Ljubo answered: "... told Ljubo to pass on to Vinko what Vinko and I were just talking about. Will arrive at your place by 1700 hours. The boss, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, will arrive and say what needs to be done regarding the work we talked about." Did you receive a message to that effect from Ljubo Bojanovic, the duty officer that morning?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first say that between the conversation that we just saw and this note in the work book, recorded at 8.30, there is a link between the two. After having talked to me, Cerovic probably spoke to Krstic or somebody else who could make a decision for the people to be transferred to Batkovic. And then he again called Ljubo Bojanovic and gave him the message that is recorded in the note, and this is also confirmed by the intercept that we can see on the screen. I'm not sure whether at any time during the day, at that time or later Ljubo conveyed that a message to me. However, I did know about the approval for all the prisoners who were kept at the Zvornik Brigade including the wounded to be transferred to Batkovic. Here a reference is made to Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. I am absolutely sure I did not see him at the command of the Zvornik Brigade in the course of that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And so that we can all see what you are looking at, can we have a look at P377. You've got the correct page, that's 795. We need to see page 177 in the e-court version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the entry you were looking at is the one that we can see at 0830, "Lieutenant-Colonel Cerovic relayed a message for commander that Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic will arrive by 1700 hours." Let's leave that behind us. The next entry is at 10.00, and that refers to a "... briefing at the brigade command with the commanders of the infantry and artillery battalions." Was there a briefing morning at 10.00?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a briefing which involved the commanders of the division battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What sort of meeting was it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the monthly work-plan, there were regular monthly briefings of the commanders of the battalions, divisions, and subordinated units and the inner circle of the brigade command. At that briefings, we analysed the combat readiness and the implementation of the plan for the previous month. The briefing that took place on that day was a combination of the regular monthly briefing and a briefing about particular activities that were very important and that had taken place over the past several days prior to the briefing itself. This briefing did take place and the emphasis was on the events that immediately preceded the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who was present?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the battalion and division commanders. And when I say "division" I mean the commander of the mixed artillery division Milos Maksimovic and the commander of the light infantry division of the anti-aircraft defence, Albert Markovic [phoen]. There was also the commander of the Podrinje Detachment, Jolovic. The assistant commanders. The Chief of Staff was there as well. The operations officer, Dragutinovic. Major Galic. Most probably the chiefs of various services. I would say that those were the people that were present at the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where was it held and how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That briefing as well as all the others was held in the ops room which was between the office of the assistant for logistics and the office of the operations organ, which means that it was on the first floor of the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was discussed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As usual, the meeting would be opened by the commander, that is me, and then the battalion commanders and the division commanders would refer -- report on the combat readiness of the battalions, the implementation of tasks. Then the command organs would discuss each their own sectors of work and submit their reports. Then the chiefs of services would state what the situation was in the staff units. The Chief of Staff would discuss command and control problems, and then at the end of the meeting I would summarise everything that was said and issue tasks for the forthcoming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you didn't fully answer my earlier question. How long did all that take?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly how long it took, but at least an hour, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting everyone would go back to their units and the command organs would go back to their officers [as interpreted] and the Chief of Staff Obrenovic and myself would go to our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm just curious, General Pandurevic, you appear to be talking in the conditional tense throughout the whole of that. Is that what did happen? Did you go back to your office or offices with Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we went back, Obrenovic and myself went to my office and the rest went to their own places. This would be the past tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, I thought you probably did. Which office did you go to with Major Obrenovic, yours or his?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the brigade commander's office, that is the office where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what did the two of you talk about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to a topic that we talked about on the 18th of July. We were particularly interested in knowing how come that nobody from the corps command in the meantime had called back or sent a return document requesting more detailed information from us, or to inform us about anything that had to do with that. We also talked about how come that none of the battalion commanders or those present at the meetings did not mention the prisoners of war at all, or referred to the events relating to the executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just so that we understand the position. Between the 18th and July and this meeting on the morning of the 23rd, where had Dragan Obrenovic been?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th, Dragan Obrenovic was at the command of the 4th Battalion in Balkovica, and for the most part until the 23rd he was in charge of the search of the terrain in Baljkovici-Planinici-Tarabic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where had he been spending his nights?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time he would spend the night in the barracks and sometimes at home, I'm not sure which night he was where.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Had you had an opportunity before this to speak to him about what he had told you earlier again?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 18th and the conversation in Baljkovica, this was our third conversation or our fourth conversation relating to the prisoners and their fate. Also the conversation that we had on the 23rd after the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did he have any further information to that which he had given you on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have any special additional information. He simply stated his opinion and his thoughts about the events that were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what was his opinion and what were his thoughts?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He simply said something like what happened, how did it happen, how is it that it happened precisely here. I happen to agree with him and I asked him what did he think, what did he suggest in terms of what we should do next, and I mentioned the interim combat report that I had sent on the 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But what did you mention about it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him and I think in the meantime he had also seen that report, I told him what I had written in the report and that I was surprised that the corps command didn't react to that. We agreed that at that point in time that was all that we could do. I was expecting any day to return to Zepa and to talk to Krstic personally, among other things, about this matter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What sort of mood were you in when you had this discussion with Obrenovic on the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to describe the whole situation. The anger, the rage, the nausea a person feels at a time like that. It was our conclusion to the effect that where is this leading us, what sort of a brain could have decided something like that, but according to the information that we had, we knew that the order had come from General Mladic. And I don't know if it was me or him who said that this is not going to take us far, this manner of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did in that discussion express your anger or rage? And if so, how?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I said something to the effect who put this in our laps? Who placed this in Zvornik, because if something like this happens in the area of Zvornik, everybody would logically assume that this was something that was committed by the Zvornik Brigade, leaving aside the gravity of the crime itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you discuss what action you should take?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did think about that too, whether to conduct an investigation and what sort of investigation, and then at the time we concluded that the report that we had sent on the 18th represented at that stage the most that we were able to do, and that after I personally meet General Krstic, we would be able to know if we would do something more or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What were the main reasons for that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already earlier today I said what I knew about that, and the information was discussed at this meeting also, and we understood that it would be illusory to conduct an investigation in the usual way that it should be conducted. It was also our position that sometimes the truth, if it comes too early, can have more negative consequences than if it were to be a bit delayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You said that one of the things you discussed with Obrenovic at your meeting was the fact that nobody in the briefing had mentioned prisoners or killings. Did you raise it with those at that briefing?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't raise that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was that a deliberate decision?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why did you not raise the question with the assembled commanders at the meeting on the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meantime, I didn't receive any information back from the corps command. I wasn't able to launch or initiate such a major issue in front of such a large number of people for a number of reasons; one of them being that matters like that when the concealment of evidence is possible and other kinds of actions are possible, should not be then launched other than in a much smaller circle and in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you mind if we lose a couple of minutes today because that really is the end of a topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not at all. So we are going to finish here today. We reassemble tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 10th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
